item.title: Japanese supertanker becomes first to exit Gulf since Iran war began
item.description: A sanctioned Russian oligarch's superyacht and a Japanese crude oil supertanker have each transited the blockaded Strait of Hormuz in recent days, underscoring cracks in the competing maritime restrictions imposed by the United States and Iran since war broke out in late February.

item.title: DOJ indicts former FBI director Comey a second time
item.description:
The Department of Justice has indicted former FBI Director James Comey for the second time, CNN reported on Tuesday, citing two sources familiar with the matter. The specific charges in the new indictment have not yet been publicly disclosed.

The move marks an escalation in the Trump administration's legal pursuit of Comey, whose first indictment in September 2025 was dismissed after a federal judge found the prosecutor who brought the case had been unlawfully appointed.

item.title: Trump claims Iran in 'state of collapse,' wants Hormuz reopened
item.description:
President Donald Trump claimed on Tuesday that Iran has asked the United States to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, portraying Tehran as desperate to end a naval blockade that has choked its economy amid a fragile ceasefire between the two nations.

"Iran has just informed us that they are in a 'State of Collapse.' They want us to 'Open the Hormuz Strait,' as soon as possible, as they try to figure out their leadership situation," Trump posted on Truth Social, adding that he believes Iran will be able to resolve its internal issues.

item.title: Cursor AI agent wiped startup's database in 9 seconds, founder says
item.description: An AI coding agent wiped a startup's entire production database and all its backups in a single API call lasting nine seconds, leaving car rental businesses scrambling to serve customers with no booking records over the weekend.

item.title: U.S. Marines board cargo ship in Arabian Sea to enforce Iran blockade
item.description: U.S. Marines on Tuesday boarded and searched a commercial vessel in the Arabian Sea suspected of attempting to reach Iran in violation of the American naval blockade, the military said, before releasing the ship after confirming it was not headed to an Iranian port.

item.title: Amazon to offer OpenAI models on AWS after Microsoft exclusivity ends
item.description:
Microsoft and OpenAI announced on Monday that their partnership has been restructured, ending Microsoft's exclusive license to OpenAI's models and products — a change that immediately opened the door for Amazon to begin distributing OpenAI's technology through its cloud platform.

Hours after the announcement, Amazon CEO Andy Jassy posted on X calling it a "very interesting announcement," adding that the company is "excited to make OpenAI's models available directly to customers on Bedrock in the coming weeks, alongside the upcoming Stateful Runtime Environment."

item.title: Ships cross Strait of Hormuz as U.S.-Iran standoff stalls
item.description:
Four civilian ships passed through the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, including a Japanese supertanker carrying some two million barrels of Saudi crude oil, even as competing U.S. and Iranian blockades continue to choke one of the world's most vital waterways two months into the conflict.

The transits came as the Trump administration weighed a new Iranian proposal to mutually lift restrictions on the strait in exchange for delaying nuclear talks, a deal that appeared unlikely to gain traction in Washington.

item.title: King Charles urges unity in rare address to Congress
item.description:
King Charles III addressed a joint session of the U.S. Congress on Tuesday, calling on the two nations to defend their shared democratic values and declaring that "time and again, our two countries have always found ways to come together," in a rare royal speech to American lawmakers that carried unmistakable undertones about the strains testing the transatlantic alliance.

The address — only the second by a British monarch before Congress, after Queen Elizabeth II's 1991 speech — came on the second day of a four-day state visit and at a moment of acute tension between Washington and London over the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran and President Donald Trump's sharp criticism of NATO allies.

item.title: Tropical forest loss fell 36% in 2025, but fires threaten gains
item.description:
The world lost 4.3 million hectares of tropical primary rainforest in 2025 — an area roughly the size of Denmark — representing a 36% decline from the record-shattering losses of 2024, according to new data released Wednesday by the World Resources Institute's Global Forest Watch platform.

The findings, produced by the University of Maryland's GLAD Lab, show that strong government action can curb deforestation. But researchers warn the drop may reflect fewer fires rather than durable progress, and that loss levels remain about 70% higher than what is needed to meet the 2030 goal of halting deforestation.

item.title: Europe hit record wildfires and Arctic heatwaves in 2025, new climate report finds
item.description:
Europe endured its second-worst heatwave season on record in 2025, with extreme heat stretching from the Mediterranean to the Arctic Circle and wildfires burning the largest area ever documented, according to the European State of the Climate report released on Tuesday by the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) and the World Meteorological Organization (WMO).

The report, drawing on contributions from around 100 scientists, found that at least 95 percent of Europe experienced above-average annual temperatures in 2025, with the United Kingdom, Norway, and Iceland recording their hottest years on record. A three-week heatwave in sub-Arctic Fennoscandia pushed temperatures above 30°C within the Arctic Circle, while southern and eastern Spain endured up to 50 additional days where temperatures felt like 32°C or higher.

item.title: EU finds Meta failed to block under-13s from Instagram, Facebook
item.description:
The European Commission on Wednesday issued preliminary findings that Meta violated the Digital Services Act by failing to stop children under 13 from using Facebook and Instagram, escalating one of the bloc's most closely watched enforcement cases against a major tech company.

The Commission said Meta had failed to "diligently identify, assess and mitigate the risks of minors under 13 years old accessing their services," despite its own terms and conditions setting 13 as the minimum age for both platforms. If the findings are upheld, Meta could face fines of up to 6% of its global annual revenue.

item.title: Adelaide researchers map path to turning plastic into hydrogen fuel
item.description:
Researchers at Adelaide University have laid out a roadmap for converting plastic waste into hydrogen and other clean fuels using sunlight, advancing a technology they say could address both pollution and energy challenges simultaneously.

The study, published this week in the journal Chem Catalysis, examines how a process known as solar-driven photoreforming uses light-activated materials called photocatalysts to break down plastics at relatively low temperatures, producing hydrogen — a zero-emissions fuel — along with syngas, acetic acid, and even diesel-range hydrocarbons.

item.title: Asian stocks rise, oil falls after UAE quits OPEC
item.description:
The United Arab Emirates announced on Tuesday that it will leave OPEC and OPEC+ effective May 1, ending nearly six decades of membership in the oil cartel and sending ripples through global energy and equity markets.

Asian stocks mostly advanced on Wednesday despite the upheaval, while oil prices fell as traders assessed the implications of losing one of OPEC's largest producers. The Kospi rose 0.3% in Seoul, Hong Kong's Hang Seng climbed about 1%, and the Shanghai Composite edged up 0.3%, according to the Associated Press. India's Sensex gained 0.4%, while Australia's S&P/ASX 200 dipped 0.3% and Taiwan's Taiex fell 0.6%. Japanese markets were closed for a holiday. Brent crude and U.S. benchmark crude both declined in early Wednesday trading.

item.title: France unveils roadmap to end all fossil fuel use by 2050
item.description: France on Tuesday presented what it called a "first of its kind" national roadmap to phase out coal by 2030, oil by 2045, and natural gas by 2050, laying out a comprehensive timeline for weaning Europe's second-largest economy off fossil fuels entirely.

item.title: Iran tensions shadow White House state dinner for British royals
item.description: President Donald Trump and King Charles III celebrated the enduring alliance between their nations at a White House state dinner on Tuesday evening, capping a day of pomp and diplomacy that included the king's rare address to a joint session of Congress. The White House marked the occasion by posting a photo of the two leaders on social media with the caption "TWO KINGS," a move that drew widespread attention.

item.title: China's solar capacity set to surpass coal for first time in 2026
item.description: The United States and China are both on track to add record amounts of clean energy capacity in 2026, driven by falling technology costs and surging electricity demand, even as the two countries face divergent policy headwinds that threaten to slow the pace of the transition.

item.title: Trump orders extended Iran blockade after rejecting Tehran's proposal
item.description:
President Trump has effectively rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, instead directing aides to prepare for a prolonged naval blockade of Iranian ports, according to The Wall Street Journal. The decision, reached during a Monday Situation Room meeting with his national security team, marks an escalation in the two-month-old conflict that has disrupted roughly one-fifth of the world's oil supply.

Iran's proposal, first reported by Axios and The Associated Press on Sunday, offered to jointly reopen the strait and extend the current ceasefire while postponing discussions on Tehran's nuclear program to a later date. Sources told CBS News that the deal was conditional on the U.S. lifting its blockade of Iranian ports.

item.title: Putin proposes Victory Day truce in Ukraine during call with Trump
item.description:
President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin spoke by phone on Wednesday in a wide-ranging conversation that touched on the war in Iran, peace efforts in Ukraine, and the recent shooting at the White House Correspondents' Dinner, according to the Kremlin.

The call, which lasted roughly 90 minutes, was confirmed by Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov, who told reporters that Putin proposed ideas for resolving the Iran conflict and expressed readiness to declare a truce in Ukraine for Russia's Victory Day celebrations on May 9. It was the first known direct conversation between the two leaders since a similar call in March.

item.title: Perovskite device sets records as both solar cell and LED
item.description: A single perovskite device has achieved world-record performance in both solar energy conversion and light emission, a feat that had previously been accomplished only by costly single-crystal gallium arsenide. The study, published in Joule, describes a diode that converts sunlight to electricity at 26.7% efficiency and emits light with an external quantum efficiency of roughly 31%, demonstrating that the long-standing divide between photovoltaic and LED device design is an engineering problem rather than a physical limitation.

item.title: London stabbing of 2 Jewish men declared terrorist attack
item.description:
Two Jewish men were stabbed on the streets of north London on Wednesday morning in what police have formally declared a terrorist incident, marking the latest in a series of antisemitic attacks to strike the capital's Jewish community.

The attack occurred at approximately 11:16 a.m. on Highfield Avenue in Barnet, near Golders Green, a neighborhood home to one of London's largest Jewish populations. The victims, aged 76 and 34, suffered knife wounds and were taken to hospital, where they are reported to be in stable condition.
